recipes.name: Savory Apple Cider Beef Stew
ingredients_raw: 1 pound beef stew meat, cut into bite-size pieces
2 small Fuji apples - peeled, cored, and chopped

steps.text: Combine beef with flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, black pepper, and 1/8 teaspoon thyme in a bowl; toss to coat evenly.

Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add beef; cook until browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in apple cider with a wooden spoon while scraping the browned bits of food off the bottom of the pan; reduce heat to medium low, and simmer until beef is tender, about 1 hour.
Add carrots, potatoes, apples, onion, water, celery, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon thyme to the pot; continue cooking until vegetables are tender, about 30 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Apple Cider Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: This apple cider beef stew combines the flavor of apple with tender beef, carrots, and potatoes for a comforting, naturally sweet and savory stew.

review.reviewBody: This was wonderful and unique, perfect for fall season. I did feel that the cider made it overly sweet, so i added savory flavors such a bay leave, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, a dash of worcester sauce, and basil. Also, if i did it again, i would use beef stock as the addition at the end instead of water. Sweet potatoes were also a wonderful addition to the flavor mix. Will definitely be cooking every year for the fall!
I thought it was very tasty. I did add beef broth, thanks to the reviews. Thanks for the recipe and the reviews!

It’s a very nice recipe, though I made some tweaks. I had read that the flavour was too weak, so I added a beef stock cube, left out the water and put in a whole teaspoon of pepper. The result was flavourful and had a bit of a kick which I personally like.

I'm not usually a big stew fan, but this was great. I used part of a pork butt -that's what I had-instead of beef. I kept the other ingredients pretty much the same and followed the instructions(mostly). Cut the pork into cubes about the size of stew meat and browned them. I think next time I'll put the potatoes in earier, they were still a bit hard. But no matter, the flavor was great and the meat juicy.
Fantastic! Easy! Refreshing change from the same ol' same ol' and my family loved it.
Good but I could have used a stronger taste.

Outstanding!! The only thing I did differently was to use 1/2 cup of white wine to deglaze the pan because who doesn’t want to scrape up all those delicious bits with a little wine? So, instead of adding the full cup of water as instructed I only added 1/2 cup of water. This was by far the most flavorful stew I have ever made. I did not find this to be overly sweet with all of the cider nor did I find it to be bland in anyway. Definitely a keeper.

I made this during a Nor'easter, so I used my oven to cook it low & slow, at about 270F for 8 hours in a dutch oven. I used 5 McIntosh apples (they're my favorite apples), added extra carrots & celery, & added about 1 teaspoon of dried Tarragon. I skipped the step of browning the meat. I checked & stirred the stew about every hour, & added more cider when too much liquid had evaporated. The result: tender beef infused w/ wonderful apple flavor & delicious vegetables in tangy yet savory broth. Slow cooking thickened the stew without having to add flour.
I made this with 1 lb of cubed pork and 1 lb of hot Italian sausage. Also thickened it with a jar of pork gravy. The combination of sweet cider and the savory sausage made for an exceptional dish.

Wow, it’s so amazing! I doubled the recipe besides the meat so that there would be plenty! I added the same amount of thyme though(just forgot to add it the second time) and a sweet potato instead of extra carrots (ran out). I wish I would have had more apples... they, the broth and the meat were the best!! Sooo good! The soup is genius, and the beef goes surprisingly well with the broth. Don’t be afraid of the sweet.. it works— it is an apple cider soup after all!
